chapter_theme: Sivavakkiyar reads the five-letter mantra (சிவாயம், அஞ்செழுத்து) as a thing inside the body and the mind rather than a formula learned from books: it is the letters A and U blossoming, the fire in the triangle, the serpent's mouth, the embryo in the womb. Around this run the refrains 'isn't it one?' (ஒன்றலோ) and 'it became Sivayam' (சிவாயமே): temple, tank, fire, air, senses and worlds are all one thing, and the body that knows this is itself the vision. The chapter closes by denying that letters, soul, elements, senses and scriptures are beginningless; only the truth mingled with all of them is.
structure_note: The verses alternate between coded accounts of the five letters and the inner fire (1339, 1341, 1343 to 1346, 1348, 1349, 1352 to 1355, 1359 to 1362) and plain-spoken rebukes and questions to the confused (1340, 1342, 1347, 1350, 1351, 1356 to 1358, 1360, 1363). Many verses end on the refrain சிவாயமே; 1343 and 1344 share a last line, as do the pairs 1347/1357/1358 with the question ஒன்றலோ.

1339.reading: Melting space, the five letters and the rhythm of bindu and nada, melting the drop and mixing in ghee until everything is pure, and knowing the two both in space and in that act, Sivayam became clear by the nature that passes beyond space.
1339.nuance: The verse is an alchemical figure for an inner event: உருக்கி (melting) is said of space and of தளி, which can be a shrine or a drop, and நெய் (ghee) suggests an oblation. இருவர் (the two) is traditionally Siva and Shakti, or the sun and moon of the yogic body. What the plain sense of the melting is remains open.

1340.reading: You people confused by the mantras you have learned, will you recite them when you are dead? The mantras are within you, and so are you who valued them; the mantra is the five letters of the mind.
1340.nuance: The second line is the hinge: a mantra held in memory dies with the one who learned it. மனத்தின் ஐந்து எழுத்து relocates the pancakshara from speech to the mind, which the rest of the chapter develops.

1341.reading: Beyond the three regions, in the work of the three-eyed one, within the supreme awareness the spring is Sivayam, the five letters; after the supreme self arose and the pillar became everywhere, this side draws in and everything became the linga.
1341.nuance: முப்புறம் (three regions) may be the three worlds or the three cities Siva burned; தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva and, in yogic reading, the spine. உற்புனம் is obscure, perhaps a spring. The last line turns the installed linga into the whole, which pairs with the chapter's mockery of temple stone.

1342.reading: Is the dancing jiva the five elements, the light that joined them, or the root that frolics? Is it what stood and saw the land, or the learning the tongue acquired? Having seen the house of release and burst open, it became the open space.
1342.nuance: The questions deny each candidate: the soul is not the elements, nor the light, nor what it has seen, nor what it has learned. வெட்டவெளி (bare open space) is the Siddhars' word for the final state, and வீடு கண்டு puts seeing release before becoming it.

1343.reading: When the form took shape, the truth that stood level with the jiva, and in anything that has rightness, is Sivayam, the five letters; after settling, pressing and subsiding into single enjoyment, the Lord who carries the skull arose from the thought.
1343.nuance: கருத்து is thought or intention, but beside கரு (womb) in the next verse it may also mean the womb; the Lord then 'arises from the womb' with each birth, or 'arises in the thought' of the one absorbed. ஏகபோகம் (single enjoyment) is read as union. The last line is shared with 1344.

1344.reading: When conceived and risen it became the lotus seat; when conceived and risen it became the causes; when conceived and risen it became two eyes to see; and from the thought arose the Lord who carries the skull.
1344.nuance: கருத்தரித்து is literally 'holding the embryo', so the verse follows the embryo as it becomes the lotus seat (the base centre, in yogic reading), the causal faculties and the eyes. The Lord then arises in the womb, or in the thought; see 1343. The verse makes embryology and theology one story.

1345.reading: The fire that is in the triangle, in the six, two and eight; the jiva that is the five letters, blossoming with the letter A set in it; the truth that is the light and the beginningless truth: becoming that and becoming itself, it will hide as void.
1345.nuance: மூன்றுகோணம் (triangle) is traditionally the base centre where the fire sleeps, and the numbers are read as petals or centres; none of this is in the text. அவலமாய் can mean 'as void' or 'in distress', and the verb மறைந்திடும் (hides, vanishes) leaves open whether the hiding is the Lord's or the soul's.

1346.reading: Our Lord who was born and rose, in the open space of the holy stage, became the four directions through the mouth of the hanging serpent; after it passed the three cities as three and three rings, the sound of that letter, born and risen, stood everywhere.
1346.nuance: நான்ற பாம்பு (the hanging serpent) is the coiled power in yogic reading, and திருவரங்கம் is both Srirangam and 'holy stage'. மூன்றுமூன்று வளையம் (rings in threes) and அவ்வின் ஓசை (the sound of the letter A, or 'that sound') are coded; the plain sense is that one sound fills everything.

1347.reading: Isn't it one everywhere? Aren't the fourteen worlds one, here and there one, the beginningless one, the standing things and what bears them one? Sivayam arose in your share and ours alike.
1347.nuance: ஒன்றலோ (isn't it one?) is the refrain of 1357 and 1358 too. உங்கள் எங்கள் பங்கினில் (in your share and ours) is a jab at the caste and sect divisions that the poet attacks elsewhere: the same thing arose in both.

1348.reading: The light that dances in the sky is the root of the fire; sky and self blossomed with the fierce one set in them; setting the body in the pit of the sky and melting it, Sivayam sat with the First in the sky.
1348.nuance: அம்பரம் is space and also the cloth, and the hall of the dance is heard behind ஆடும் சோதி. அகோரம் (Aghora, the fierce face of Siva) returns in 1355 as something 'set' before blossoming. அம்பரக் குழி (the pit of space) is read by tradition as the space in the crown.

1349.reading: The unfading flower blossomed, with the bee's hum on the tongue; running, taking form, it blossomed as the letter U; dancing and dancing until the body was caught within and passed, we walk about joined: that is the form in which the guru dwelt.
1349.nuance: வாடிலாத பூ (the unfading flower) is the inner lotus, and the bee's hum on the tongue is the mantra as sound. உகாரம் is the U of Om. The last line makes the guru's state the end of the whole process rather than its beginning.

1350.reading: Did it sprout from the root that was let go, or did it stand melting that root? Did the jiva that reached out see the fourteen worlds? Is it the light of Sadasiva standing as a flat form? Will those who know the round house become the gods of the sky?
1350.nuance: விட்டடி விரைத்ததோ is obscure and may be corrupt. வட்டவீடு (the round house) recurs in 1351; tradition takes it as the circle of space in the head or the sphere of the whole, and the questions may be rhetorical denials or genuine.

1351.reading: The light the gods fill is in the human embryo, and all the gods of heaven come and settle inside it; after knowing the round house of sky and earth, they became the rubies that fill the whole heaven.
1351.nuance: The claim is that the gods are inside the human embryo, not above it. வட்டவீடு, the round house, carries over from 1350; here it spans heaven and earth, so the body as cosmos is in view. Who 'became the rubies' is unclear: the knowers or the gods.

1352.reading: If, holding the breath to twelve and reaching the five colours, one stays standing within the space and settles in another place, the jiva moves in the place that is the head; those who thought on this and searched it out became the supreme Brahman.
1352.nuance: பன்னிரண்டு கால் நிறுத்தி is read as holding the breath (கால், wind) to a measure of twelve, the span the breath travels in yogic texts; it could also be twelve feet or supports. பஞ்சவண்ணம் (five colours) is the elements, or the coloured lights seen in meditation. சென்னி (the head) is the one plain body-place.

1353.reading: Seeing the summit with the eyes shut, where did one see the truth? If the human mingles inside the upper storey, even the door of spittle becomes single enjoyment; the green Mal and the Lord are Sivayam that spread beyond.
1353.nuance: மச்சு மாளிகை (the upper storey of the mansion) is read as the head, and எச்சிலான வாசல் (the spittle door) as the mouth; so the verse says the mouth itself becomes union when the mind is in the crown. பச்சை மால் (green or dark Vishnu) and ஈசன் being one Sivayam repeats the poet's refusal of sect.

1354.reading: Set in the mouth, in the sound of the letters of the good hum; the temple set and the tank dried there in the branch; the body made by inquiry, the jiva set from no beginning and the fire the wind let loose: all of it grew as Sivayam.
1354.nuance: நல்லுரிசை (the good hum, or 'good rishi') is unclear, and கொம்பிலே உலர்ந்ததும் (dried in the branch, or horn) is obscure; it may picture the inner tank drying up as the fire rises. The verse gathers mantra, body, soul and breath into one growth.

1355.reading: Uttering the letter as the root of the beginningless fire, opening the letter too and blossoming with the fierce one set in it, after passing so that the inner hand in the earth-row was caught, Sivayam sat with the First in the letter.
1355.nuance: அட்சரம் (the letter) appears in every line, and the verse is a cipher for how the uttered letter becomes the inner fire. மட்சரத்தில் உட்கரம் is obscure; மட்சரம் may be a corrupt form. அகோரமிட்டு அலர்ந்ததும் repeats 1348.

1356.reading: You are confused in mind by temples and tanks, by gurus taken on their badges, and by the rest; if you know and realise the Cowherd and Hara, it is like sitting down with your mother and your father.
1356.nuance: குறியினிற் குருக்களாய் is gurus known by their marks, the outward signs rather than knowledge. மாயிலும் மடியிலும் is unclear (peacock and lap? or some other pair of objects of confusion). ஆயன் (the cowherd) is Vishnu beside Hara, both to be known as one; the mother-and-father image returns in 1384.

1357.reading: Isn't the temple one everywhere, and the tanks and their waters one? Aren't fire and air one, and isn't Siva there one too? Isn't the jiva that became everything and abides one? Those who know this body become the vision itself.
1357.nuance: The list moves from temple and tank through the elements to Siva and the soul, all answered by the same ஒன்றலோ. காயம் ஈது அறிந்த பேர்கள் (those who know this body) says where the oneness is known: not in the many temples but in the one body.

1358.reading: Ears, eyes, nose and mouth: isn't what mixed them one? What was raised with light and the five pleasures: aren't they one? Didn't the recited scriptures arise from one? Those who know the house of nada become Lords.
1358.nuance: The senses, their pleasures and the sastras are traced to one source. நாதவீடு (the house of sound) is the inner place of nada, and நாதர் (Lords, masters) answers it with a pun: those who know the house of nada are nathar.

1359.reading: The letter mingled within the letter that rose as A, and the mantra that rose as Sa, were in the abode of Sambhu; you people confused by the maya that rose as Ma, what rose as U took form together with A: that is the truth.
1359.nuance: Each line opens with a letter: அவ், சவ், மவ், உவ். Tradition reads ம as the letter of malam and maya (so மவ்வுதித்த மாய்கை), சி or ச as Siva, and அ and உ as the two that make Om. சம்புளத்து is unclear, perhaps 'in Sambhu's place'. The verse gives the letters, not their keys.

1360.reading: In the letter called A, did the other letters end? Did the letter A arise from the letter A? Did U and A stand well joined? You jnanis free of change, you must expound this at length.
1360.nuance: The questions concern the parts of Om and whether A contains, generates or joins the rest; the verse does not answer them and asks the jnanis to. விகாரமற்ற (without change) marks the jnani as one past the changes the letters stand for.

1361.reading: Shakti is your body; the wavering jiva within it is Siva. Madmen, there is nothing more to babble beyond this. Five purities, one hall, a space beyond words; to become Shakti and Siva and be cool is the truth.
1361.nuance: The first line is the plainest statement in the chapter of the body-as-Shakti doctrine: the body is her, the soul is him. சுத்தி ஐந்து கூடம் ஒன்று (five purities, one hall) is coded, perhaps the five elements purified in the one body. தண்மை (coolness) names the end as calm rather than power.

1362.reading: In the channel of the seed, in the embryo of blood, on the mound that sprouted at the three-cornered gate, within the true square, shining in the true body as the lamp of knowledge, the mantra uttered is Om Nama Sivaya.
1362.nuance: சுக்கிலம் and சுரோணிதம் are the male and female seeds in Siddha medicine, so the verse places the mantra in conception itself. முச்சதுர வாசல் and மெய்ச்சதுரம் (the three-cornered gate, the true square) are body-places tradition maps onto the base centre; the text does not say which.

1363.reading: The letters are not beginningless; the soul is not beginningless; the elements that entered and the senses are not beginningless; the worthy books and the scriptures are not beginningless; the truth that stands level and mingled with all of them is the beginningless.
1363.nuance: ஆத்துமம் அனாதி அல்ல denies the soul a beginningless existence, which sets the verse against Saiva Siddhanta, where soul, Lord and bond are all eternal. Read with 1361, the soul is Siva within and so has no separate eternity; the verse may also simply rank everything named below the one truth.

links.note: Tirumular says the knowing soul, the Lord and the bond are all beginningless; Sivavakkiyar says the soul is not beginningless, only the truth mingled with all things is. The conflict holds if ஆத்துமம் means the individual soul of Siddhanta; it softens if the poet means that the soul has no being apart from Siva, who alone is eternal.

Tirumular says the five letters protect the soul when Death lays hand on it; Sivavakkiyar asks whether the mantras one has learned can be recited when one is dead, and locates the real mantra in the mind. He does not deny the five letters, but moves them from learned speech to inner knowing, which limits what the recited formula can do.

Both make the body the temple: Tirumular's heart is the great temple, the flesh the shrine and the soul the linga; Sivavakkiyar says temple, tank, fire, air and Siva are one and those who know this body become the vision itself.
Tirumular says Parashakti stood as his body and life and became his awareness; Sivavakkiyar states the same as doctrine: Shakti is your body, and the jiva within it is Siva.

Both count letters without giving the key: Tirumular says by one letter he became all, by two he is two, by three the light springs up; Sivavakkiyar asks whether A holds the rest, arose from itself, or joined with U, and leaves the answer to the jnanis.

Tirumular says the Lord is not in the mansion, hall, temple or ascetic's garb but in the heart of those free of longing; Sivavakkiyar says temples, tanks and gurus known by their badges only confuse, and knowing Hara is like sitting with one's own parents.

source_issues: 1350 line 1 (விட்டடி விரைத்ததோ) and 1355 line 3 (மட்சரத்தில் உட்கரம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1343 and 1344 share their last line (கருத்தினின்று உதித்ததே கபாலம் ஏந்தும் நாதனே); this looks deliberate, but one may have borrowed it from the other.
